title: Fluorometric Method for Detecting Cell Death in 3D Intestinal Organoids
author: Konstantin J. Bode
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.78vhrw6
materials: Start plate reader and measurement software (Tecan). Tecan

steps.title: Plate crypts in Matrigel
steps.instruction: Plate 200–300 intestinal crypts per well in a clear 96‑well plate using 8 µL of Matrigel or BME; incubate 20 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, then add 80 µL of pre‑warmed complete murine intestinal organoid growth medium dropwise over the crypts.

steps.title: Incubate organoids to form cultures
steps.instruction: Allow the seeded organoids to grow for 3 days at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ before any treatment.

steps.title: Treat organoids with cytotoxin
steps.instruction: Add Staurosporine (or other test substance) to each well and incubate for at least 16 h (16:00:00) to ensure plasma‑membrane disruption. Use technical triplicates and include untreated (negative) and Staurosporine‑treated (positive) control wells.

steps.title: Inspect morphology before staining
steps.instruction: Microscopically examine organoid growth and integrity, noting any morphological differences between treated and untreated wells.

steps.title: Replace medium with staining solution
steps.instruction: Remove the treatment medium and add 80 µL of pre‑warmed, phenol‑red‑free medium to each well.

steps.title: Stain organoids with PI and Hoechst
steps.instruction: Add staining medium containing final concentrations of 10 mg mL⁻¹ Propidium Iodide and Hoechst 33342 to each well. Incubate for 30 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Microscopic fluorescence check
steps.instruction: Observe the wells under a fluorescence microscope to confirm PI and Hoechst staining before plate‑reader measurement.

steps.title: Prepare plate reader for measurement
steps.instruction: Remove the plate lid and set the reader to top‑position measurement at room temperature. Set gain using the highest‑death (PI) and lowest‑death (Hoechst) control wells so values fall between 115 and 160; readjust if needed. Allow the instrument to auto‑determine the optimal Z‑position (target 1.5×10⁶–1.6×10⁶ µm; up to 2 min).

substeps.instruction: Adjust gain to 115–160 using control wells.
Enable automatic Z‑position determination and verify values between 1.5×10⁶ and 1.6×10⁶ µm.

steps.title: Acquire fluorescence readings
steps.instruction: Measure PI fluorescence (excitation 535 nm, emission 617 nm) for all wells, then wait 30 s and measure Hoechst fluorescence (excitation 361 nm, emission 486 nm). Use 25 flashes, 20 µs integration time, 0 s lag/settle time, and a 4 × 4 measurement grid per well with a 1 mm border. Increase measurement points if organoid distribution is uneven.

steps.title: Calculate PI/Hoechst fluorescence ratio
steps.instruction: Compute the ratio of relative fluorescence units (RFU) for each well: PI/H ratio = RFU(PI) / RFU(Hoechst).

steps.title: Quantify percent cell death
steps.instruction: Determine treatment‑specific cell death [%] by dividing each sample’s PI/H ratio by the positive‑control (Staurosporine) ratio, multiplying by 100, and subtracting the untreated‑control ratio: % death = (x(sample) / z(STS)) × 100 – y(untreated).
